claim: Mutating commands returned the full DesktopSnapshot, so a slow mutation could resolve after the background dispatcher's newer snapshot and overwrite it (last-write-wins race)
UploadQueuePage used a cached-format lookup that was no longer in scope, so rendering queue rows threw a ReferenceError
Error handlers read error.message, but invoke() rejects with a raw string, so every failure showed the generic fallback text
csp was null, so the renderer ran with no Content-Security-Policy
Sign-in injected JavaScript into the Discord OAuth webview to scrape the session cookie and exchange it for a token
reqwest clients had no timeout, so a stalled connection hung the pairing-code redeem call indefinitely
Contract schemas drifted from the server OpenAPI: invalid role enum values, missing health and upload-response fields, wrong cards source enum
Game version hard-coded to ootp27 in fetch_formats, create_upload, check_duplicate and fetch_cards instead of coming from the server profile
Detected-file reuse did not require both checksum and source timestamp to match, so a regenerated export with coarse mtime inherited a previous bad format assignment
A regenerated CSV at the same path reused the previous upload job, format assignment and tournament assignment when only the source timestamp changed
Saved filename rules auto-assigned a format to the stock OOTP stats-export filename, so every regenerated export inherited that mapping
Tournament and format mappings were reused without checking the export's team count against the format's teams per tournament
Watch-root rescans deleted and recreated upload jobs, losing completed upload history across restarts
Cached format rows written by older versions lacked tournamentIdPrefix and crashed app startup when parsed
Card-list uploads were left in the stats-export-only refresh_pending state instead of completing once the server applied the list
Unchanged rescans bumped upload job updated_at, reordering the queue as if files were new
